priya: quick design review idea 1 1 :sparkles: Instead of a persistent token pill, what if we show a floating micro-toolbar on hover/focus over the streaming response? shows a tiny budget meter + actions (Stop | Regenerate | Details). aims: less visual noise, still discoverable. fig: https://figma.redwood/hoverbar-proto nate: i like less noise. question: how do we surface token info without scaring users? call it 'budget meter' or 'response progress' instead of 'tokens left'. laura: +1 to 'budget' language. microcopy suggestion: "Response progress 24 est" with tooltip: "Estimated tokens used so far; billing is based on full request". keep it short. kevin: accessibility nit: hover-only is bad. toolbar must appear on focus (tab) and be reachable by keyboard. make sure it has a visible focus ring and logical tab order. a11y-bot: Automated check: floating toolbar must be in DOM order adjacent to response for screen readers. Use aria-controls to link toolbar buttons to the response region. contrast: meter foreground fails 3:1 at small sizes. recommend thicker stroke or darker fill. priya: good point. propose behavior: default collapsed -> a small chevron on the right edge. hover/focus expands overlay anchored to the response block. on mobile, tapping chevron opens bottom sheet with actions. nate: UX question: where does regenerate live? inside overlay as a primary button. Stop should be inline and quick (so people can cancel mid-stream). maybe both appear but regen is bigger. laura: i sketched two variants: 1) inline stop button always visible, hover chevron for details+regen. 2) hover toolbar with both stop+regen. variant 1 keeps critical control visible for muscle memory. kevin: for screen readers, expose a live region announcing streaming state and token progress. sample ARIA: ```html
Streaming: 24 estimated tokens used
``` also add aria-describedby on regenerate button pointing to a short explanation. priya: love the ARIA snippet. copy decision: use 'estimated tokens used' not 'left' to avoid implying remaining quota. also add a settings toggle: Preferences > Playground > "Show response budget" with options: Always | Hover only | Off. default Hover only for existing users -> keep noise low. nate: prompt library tie-in idea: Details opens a tiny panel that maps generated tokens back to prompt lines and allows swapping in a shorter prompt template. would be super useful to troubleshoot long outputs. laura: make sure that panel is keyboard dismissible (Esc) and traps focus. it's a pattern we already have in console for quick edits. propose reusing that component to keep consistency. kevin: mobile: bottom sheet should include large Stop sticky at top, Regen below, and a compact token bar. avoid tiny targets. priya: interaction notes for engineers: animate expansion to avoid jumpiness, keep overlay width <= 420px, anchor to right edge of response block. add a small delay (120ms) before showing hover overlay to avoid flicker on fast mouse movements. nate: analytics: track interactions (hover-open, stop-click, regen-click, prompt-swap) and whether users toggle the preference. experiment behind FF: play-hoverbar-2026. a11y-bot: final accessibility checklist: focusable controls, aria-live for streaming text, contrast >= 4.5:1 for small text, focus trap for panels, Esc to dismiss, keyboard shortcut suggestion (press R to regenerate when response focused) - recommend docs. priya: next steps: laura will update figma with both variants and microcopy, nate will mock storybook components and wire up analytics, kevin will write aria spec and keyboard interactions, i'll open an experiment PR and add feature flag + settings entry. aim for small internal release in two sprints. laura: posting sketches now: https://figma.redwood/hoverbar-screens :thumbsup: nate: i'll also add a lightweight tooltip explaining the meter: "Estimate based on model and prompt length". kevin: adding a code sample for the hover toolbar anchor in our component library story.```jsx ``` priya: great work team. will file followups: RD-789 (figma), RD-790 (storybook), RD-791 (accessibility spec). feel free to ping for a 15m sync if there are conflicting constraints. a11y-bot: Thread will be auto-archived after 72 hours of inactivity (system).
